summary.text: 外 means “outside” or “external,” and is also used for “foreign.” Bronze inscriptions attest it with the sense “outside”; the interpretation of its earliest construction remains disputed.

formation.text: The formation is disputed. One analysis interprets the early graph as 卜, with a divination crack’s orientation marking “outside”; another reports 月 as a sound element in Western Zhou bronze forms. A crescent-moon interpretation is also recorded, but the evidence here does not establish it.

components.text: The early graph is analyzed as 卜, the shape of a divination crack. One interpretation reads its direction as marking “outside”; this account of the earliest graph remains disputed.

sound.text: The supplied Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms for 卜 and 外 differ substantially and do not support 卜 as a sound element here.
The supplied local Mandarin readings are 卜 bǔ and 外 wài; they do not establish an ancient sound relation.

components.text: 月 is reported as a sound element in Western Zhou bronze forms. 月 and 夕 were once drawn with the same moon-shaped graph; the later 夕 shape does not show that the component originally meant “night.”

sound_limitation.text: The similar Old Chinese forms offer a possible comparison but do not independently prove 月’s phonetic role or a complete sound-change path. A secondary transcription for 外 differs from the supplied local reconstruction.

sound.text: In the supplied Baxter–Sagart rows, 月 *[ŋ]ʷat and 外 *[ŋ]ʷˤa[t]-s are similar but not identical, offering a possible sound comparison; the secondary transcription for 外 differs.
The supplied local Mandarin rows report 月 yuè and 外 wài. Their modern readings differ and do not establish an ancient sound relation; upstream character-specific lookups were unavailable.

history.text: Paleographic accounts describe an early graph resembling 卜, Western Zhou bronze forms with 月, and later forms with 夕. These reports do not establish a continuous sequence or settle the earliest graph’s interpretation. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient inscription.
The transmitted Shuowen entry glosses 外 as “distant” and explains it through divining in the evening rather than at dawn. This old dictionary explanation does not confirm the graph’s construction.

uncertainties.text: The interpretation of the earliest graph remains disputed. 月’s reported phonetic role in bronze forms has a proposed Old Chinese sound comparison, but that comparison does not prove the role or a complete sound-change path; a secondary reconstruction for 外 also differs in notation.

senses.period: Western Zhou bronze inscriptions; precise dating unresolved
senses.text: Bronze examples use 外 for “outside,” including in contrast with 內. This is identified as the basic sense; priority among all early uses is not established.
A bronze example is reported with this use; its development from “outside” is not established.
A bronze example is reported with this kinship use; its semantic connection to “outside” is not established.
“Foreign” is a current gloss; its date and development are unresolved.

limitations.text: The reported inscriptional uses do not establish a complete chronology or semantic links among “outside,” “beyond/after,” kinship, and current “foreign.”

overview.text: 外 means “outside” or “external,” and can also mean “foreign.” Bronze inscriptions use it for “outside”; its earliest construction is disputed.

components.text: One interpretation reads 卜 as a divination crack whose direction marks “outside”; this account of the early graph remains disputed.

月 is reported as a sound element in bronze forms. Its similar but nonidentical Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese readings for 月 (*[ŋ]ʷat) and 外 (*[ŋ]ʷˤa[t]-s) make that sound role plausible, not proven; a secondary transcription for 外 differs.

relationships.text: In one reported analysis, 卜 depicts a divination crack whose direction distinguishes outside from inside in the early graph.

月 is reported as a sound element in bronze forms. The supplied Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese forms, 月 *[ŋ]ʷat and 外 *[ŋ]ʷˤa[t]-s, are similar but not identical and offer a possible sound comparison. A secondary transcription for 外 differs, and the comparison does not prove the role or a complete sound-change path.
